iconicAnchor.label: Early Material Design interface system
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The system joined bold graphic clarity, simple surfaces, iconography, components, and cross-platform rules at the shift away from skeuomorphic interfaces.

sources.title: Google's Material Design: A Look Back at Its Beginning
supports: Material Design developed a shared visual language across desktop and mobile.
The system used simple shapes, iconography, controlled shadow, and rules for surfaces and motion.

sources.title: Material Design: Secrets & Stories Behind Google's UI
supports: Material Design began with a bold minimalist aesthetic and reusable open-source system.
Its component and UX guidance demonstrates that flat interface design is a system, not a set of isolated tiles.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches flat color, icon system, component hierarchy, minimal depth, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/flat-design-ui/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
